kill_argument: The claims file over-reads the one number it reproduces and under-labels the ones it misses. The seed headline iv-return calls 0.132 'the return to a year of schooling for men whose schooling responds to proximity': the complier reading that design.estimand and the contribution say is not guaranteed on these data, here attached to a three-endogenous-regressor model for which no cited result defines nearc4's compliers. H1, the primary hypothesis, reproduced 5 of 9 primary targets, yet the seed claim first-stage and the claims first-stage-se, reduced-form-se and b3-rf-se read as plain replications with no 'not reproduced', and the count claims do not name their misses. The only pre-registered statement about the return (H3b) is 'not established'; everything positive (H3a, H4) concerns the Panel A pseudo-coefficient, and H4 is the reduced-form lower bound restated. I attacked the numbers and they held: my own numpy recomputation of B6 2SLS and its SE, the A6 robust AR set, the A6 CHR breakdown and the H5 stacked-IF interval equals the metrics to 1e-9; claims.jsonl only gained lines after check-sas-listing; every verdict flag follows from its metrics; the figure matches them.
reviewer_checks_run: After the design gate, on data/derived/card_analysis.csv with the workspace .venv (python -I, script in my scratch directory, nothing written to the workspace): B6 2SLS 0.13244376 (conv SE 0.04934142, k 30); A6 robust AR set from the quadratic [0.03951096, 0.29018696]; A6 CHR breakdown lambda - 1.959964 se_HC1 = 0.0114343621; H5 A6 D = 0.0677884, stacked-IF HC1 SE 0.0546683, interval [-0.0393595, 0.1749362]. All equal the run metrics to 1e-9 or better. No other specification, sample or variant was estimated. Also: git diff 46703df..HEAD of claims.jsonl has no removed or changed line (only the 9 diag claims and sas-ols-match added); superseded fig-chr metrics identical to the current ones; crew.py validate 0 errors, 0 warnings.

findings.text: The seed headline claim gives the replicated B6 coefficient the complier-return reading that the approved design rejects. iv-return says 'the IV estimate of the log-wage return to a year of schooling for men whose schooling responds to proximity, not the average return for all men'. design.estimand and plan.json contribution say that reading needs monotonicity and rich covariates and that 'on these data even that reading is not guaranteed' (Blandhol et al.; Tubbicke); literature-r1 L1 and literature-r2 L5 asked for no unqualified complier-weighted reading. In B6, moreover, experience and its square are also endogenous and instrumented by age, so the cited complier results (Angrist-Imbens; Kling, one endogenous regressor) do not directly define what nearc4's 'compliers' are for the schooling coefficient. The Writer copies claim texts, so this would become the paper's interpretation of its main number.
findings.evidence: claims.jsonl id iv-return; plan.json design.estimand and contribution; design.threats T10
findings.resolution: Narrow the text (no run needed): 'the 2SLS coefficient on schooling in Card's basic specification (Panel B col 6), not the average return for all men; under monotonicity and rich covariates it would be a positively weighted average of returns for men whose schooling responds to proximity, and both conditions are in doubt on these data (design.estimand)'.
findings.response: Fixed: iv-return now gives the design.estimand reading (coefficient in this linear model, not the average return; the conditional weighted-average reading needs monotonicity and rich covariates, is not guaranteed here, and with experience instrumented by age the complier results do not define whose return it weights).

findings.text: H1 misses are labelled inconsistently, including two seed-required primary targets. The verdict counts 7 misses (h1_misses: B2 first stage, B2 SE, B4, B4 SE, B1, B3, B3 SE). reduced-form, b1-fs and b3-rf say 'not reproduced'; first-stage (0.3639 vs 0.365; h1_b2_first_stage_reproduced = 0), first-stage-se (0.1024 vs 0.105), reduced-form-se (0.0173 vs 0.019) and b3-rf-se (0.0174 vs 0.019) only say '(published ...)', so they read as replications. h1-primary-reproduced (5) and h1-secondary-reproduced (19) do not name the misses, and the h1_misses metric is in no claim. The diagnosis needed beside them is also absent from these texts: the design's B2/B4 regressions are the actual first stage and an age-for-experience reduced form of the B6 2SLS, while Card's printed columns match the post hoc D4 regressions (diag-targets-reproduced = 8).
findings.evidence: claims.jsonl ids first-stage, first-stage-se, reduced-form-se, b3-rf-se, h1-primary-reproduced, h1-secondary-reproduced; runs/verdict/metrics.json h1_misses and per-target flags; runs/h1-b6/metrics.json
findings.resolution: Text-only: add 'not reproduced' to the four claims; in h1-primary-reproduced and h1-secondary-reproduced list the misses (all in Panel B cols 1-4) and point to diag-targets-reproduced as the post hoc, report-only diagnosis; say in first-stage and reduced-form which regression the value is and that Card's printed column matches D4's regression. Counts stay 5/9 and 19/22.
findings.response: Fixed: first-stage, first-stage-se, reduced-form(-se), b1-fs, b3-rf(-se) all say 'not reproduced' with the D4 pointer; h1-primary-reproduced and h1-secondary-reproduced list the misses and the post hoc D4 diagnosis (diag-targets-reproduced), which does not change the counts.

findings.text: The Kling .003 is attached to the wrong column. a5-ols-se (Table 2 col 2) says 'published 0.003, which Kling also prints'. Kling's .003 accompanies his OLS .073, the Table 2 col 5 coefficient (sources/notes.md lines 32-37 and 297; c-kling-replication), where Card prints .004. The replication settles the H1 knife-edge: the col 5 SE is 0.0036984 (HC1 0.0038682, n-denominator 0.0036800), all round to .004, so Card's .004 is reproduced and Kling's .003 is not under any of the three formulas; ols-return-se says none of this. The col 2 SE (0.0034983) is the value just inside its rounding boundary.
findings.evidence: claims.jsonl ids a5-ols-se, ols-return-se; runs/h1-b6/metrics.json ols_se, ols_se_hc1, ols_se_conv_n; sources/notes.md lines 32-37, 297
findings.resolution: Move the Kling remark to ols-return-se ('Kling prints .003; no SE formula computed here gives it') and drop it from a5-ols-se.
findings.response: Fixed: a5-ols-se no longer mentions Kling; ols-return-se puts Kling's .003 against Table 2 col 5 and says no formula gives it; new claims ols-return-se-robust and ols-return-se-n (from h1-b6) carry the HC1 and n-denominator SEs.

findings.text: The young-men OLS misses Card's Table 4 row 7 and the claim does not say so. young-ols is 0.07446 against the published 0.076 (|diff| 0.0015 > 0.0005), while young-n (2037) and young-iv (0.0944 vs 0.094; SE 0.0645 vs 0.064) match and the full-sample Table 2 col 5 OLS matches Card's SAS listing to six decimals. NOTES 'What surprised us' item 3 records it; the claim text only says '(published 0.076)', and no diagnosis is given.
findings.evidence: claims.jsonl id young-ols; runs/r-age1419/metrics.json young_ols; code/r_age1419.py (T2C5 on age76 24..29); sources/notes.md line 211
findings.resolution: Label it 'not reproduced; not diagnosed' in the claim. Do not search OLS variants for the subsample; a diagnostic would need a deviation recorded before it runs and a code round, as D4 had.
findings.response: Fixed: young-ols now says 'not reproduced; not diagnosed' (no further run), noting that N and the IV estimate of row 7 are reproduced.

findings.text: The fixed reading of r-age1419 ('reported next to the full-sample estimate with both CIs') cannot be written from macros. young_iv_lo and young_iv_hi exist as metrics (-0.0319, 0.2208; the young-men interval includes 0) but are not claims, and h1-b6 writes no CI metric for the full-sample B6 estimate at all. The Writer would have to type both intervals, which protocol 0.2 forbids.
findings.evidence: plan.json design.analysis_plan step 8; runs/r-age1419/metrics.json young_iv_lo, young_iv_hi; runs/h1-b6/metrics.json (no CI keys); claims.jsonl (no young-iv-lo/hi)
findings.resolution: Add claims young-iv-lo and young-iv-hi from the existing metrics. For the full sample, either present beta (SE) with the H3(b) sets as the intervals, or add CI metrics through a code round and a --replace rerun of h1-b6; the first is cheaper.

findings.text: A planned check that weakens the instrument-strength reading was run and left out of the claims. r-cluster computed first stages with CR1 SEs as design.analysis_plan step 10 requires; for A5 the clustered first-stage SE is 1.11 times HC1 (t 3.37, so a clustered F of about 11.4, below both H2 thresholds by more than the HC1 F), for A6 0.92. Only the reduced-form clustered results became claims. The track rule asks for every planned check to be reported, including those that weaken the result.
findings.evidence: runs/r-cluster/metrics.json a5_fs_se_cl, a5_fs_cl_ratio, a5_fs_t_cl, a6_fs_se_cl, a6_fs_t_cl; claims.jsonl (only a6/a5-rf-*-cl); runs/NOTES.md 'Metrics not turned into claims'
findings.resolution: Add claims for a5/a6 first-stage clustered SE and t (with the same 'CR1 with 18 unequal cells is not reliable in either direction' caveat), or state in the paper with macros why they are omitted.
findings.response: Fixed: new claims a6/a5-fs-se-cl, -fs-cl-ratio, -fs-t-cl, a6/a5-rf-cl-ratio and n-clusters-under30 from r-cluster; texts say the A5 clustered first-stage F is below both H2 thresholds and the A6 one between them.

findings.text: b6-kappa1 overstates what kappa_1 measures. Its text calls the largest root 'a measure of how strongly age and age squared identify the experience coefficients'. With m_W = 2 the largest root reflects only the best-identified direction of the (Y0, W) system, so it says nothing about whether exp76 and exp762 are separately well identified; and it moves with b0 (5,320 at b0 = 0.0725, 6,048 at the 2SLS estimate, 41,977 at the robust upper bound 0.498), because exp76 + ed76 = age76 - 6 lies in the instrument span (runs/NOTES.md item 9).
findings.evidence: claims.jsonl ids b6-kappa1, b6-kappa1-min; runs/h3b-subvector/metrics.json b6_kappa1_at_*, b6_kappa1_min_at_b0
findings.resolution: Reword: 'largest root kappa_1 at the 2SLS estimate, which sets the GKM19 conditional critical value (near the chi-square(1) value when kappa_1 is large); it is not a measure of how well each experience coefficient is identified'.
findings.response: Fixed: b6-kappa1 is now described as the GKM19 conditioning statistic, reflecting only the best-identified direction and varying with b0; b6-kappa1-min says the same.
